The size depends entirely on what fraction of the week is currently changeover and how sequence-dependent it is; a plant running long campaigns has little to gain here and should not buy it.
where_it_helps.failure_mode: The schedule is arithmetically optimal and nobody runs it, because it violated a constraint that was never captured. A schedule that is ninety-five per cent right and untrusted delivers nothing at all — the planner quietly goes back to the spreadsheet and the licence renews for two more years before anyone says so out loud.

where_it_helps.name: Demand forecasting and forecast-value-added review
where_it_helps.the_work: A demand planner builds a statistical baseline, applies overrides from sales and account input, and passes the result into the master schedule and long-lead purchasing. In most plants nobody measures whether the overrides help.
where_it_helps.what_it_does: Hierarchical models that use promotion calendars, pricing, customer EDI signals and calendar effects, reconciled across the product and customer hierarchy. The quieter and often larger contribution is forecast-value-added analysis: showing which human overrides improved accuracy and which degraded it. It is common in such reviews to find that a material share of overrides make the forecast worse — measure it on your own history rather than assuming it either way.
where_it_helps.what_it_needs: Shipment history separated from order history, a product hierarchy stable across renames and supersessions, promotion and price history that was actually recorded, and censored-demand handling — you cannot observe demand you were unable to supply, and treating stockout weeks as low demand teaches the model to under-forecast exactly where it hurt.
where_it_helps.what_it_saves: Estimate: accuracy gains concentrate at aggregate and family level, where they translate into safety stock and expedite freight rather than into service level. Order-of-magnitude, a few points of aggregate error is worth meaningful working capital on a long-lead-time product and close to nothing on a short one.
where_it_helps.failure_mode: Improving accuracy at SKU-week where noise dominates, publishing the improvement, and changing no downstream decision. On intermittent and lumpy demand — the spares and low-runner lines that clog most plants — sophisticated methods rarely beat simple ones, and a backtest claiming otherwise usually leaked future information through the hierarchy or the promotion flags.

where_it_helps.name: Predictive maintenance
where_it_helps.the_work: Maintenance is planned by calendar or runtime against an OEM-derived PM schedule, a reliability engineer investigates after the fact, and the technicians already know which machine is sounding wrong. Condition monitoring, where it exists, is a quarterly vibration route walked with a handheld collector.
where_it_helps.what_it_does: It is sold as remaining-useful-life prediction across the plant. What actually works is narrower and older: condition monitoring with physics-based features on rotating equipment — bearing fault frequencies, motor current signature analysis, oil analysis, thermography — plus anomaly detection on a genuinely well-instrumented asset. Where there is a fleet of identical assets with real failure history, supervised prediction of a specific mode is achievable.
where_it_helps.what_it_needs: The binding constraint is failure history, not sensors and not modelling. Supervised prediction of a failure mode needs, as a rule of thumb rather than a threshold, tens of examples of that mode on that asset class, dated to the functional failure rather than to the work-order close. Most plants have single digits, partly because the PM programme is working — good maintenance deliberately destroys the data the model wants. It also needs high-rate time-synchronised signals, work orders coded to failure mode rather than "fixed it", and operating context so the model can tell a fault from a recipe change.
where_it_helps.what_it_saves: Estimate: on a real fleet of identical assets with documented failure history, a reduction in unplanned downtime on that asset class, worth the line's contribution rate times the hours avoided — and only on a line where those hours were not recoverable elsewhere in the week. On a mixed plant of one-off machines, typically nothing beyond what a disciplined vibration route and an oil analysis programme already deliver, and that programme costs a fraction of the platform.
where_it_helps.failure_mode: Alarm fatigue first: the detector fires on every start-up, changeover and recipe change, maintenance stops looking inside a month, and the dashboard stays live for years as a monument. Then the evaluation problem, which is worse and rarely mentioned — you intervene on every alarm, so you never observe whether the machine would have failed, and the model can never be scored. Both sides then argue from anecdote, and the vendor wins that argument because they brought slides.

where_it_does_not.claim: Predictive maintenance across the whole plant, using the data already in your historian
where_it_does_not.why_not: Two independent blockers, either of which is fatal. The historian stores tags at one-minute or thirty-second averages, or on deadband compression, for control and trending; the frequency content that carries a bearing or gear fault signature lives in the kilohertz range and is destroyed by that averaging before it is ever written — an overall vibration value is not a spectrum and cannot be turned back into one. And the failure labels do not exist: work orders record what was replaced and when the job was closed, not when the asset functionally failed, so even with perfect signals there is nothing to train against. A vendor who does not ask to see your work-order failure coding in the first meeting is not going to find this out until month six, by which time the subscription has renewed.

where_it_does_not.claim: A digital twin, or an AI root-cause engine, that will find the drivers of your yield loss in existing process data
where_it_does_not.why_not: The variables that actually move yield are mostly unmeasured — incoming material lot chemistry, ambient humidity and temperature at the cell, tool wear between offsets, operator technique on a manual step. Worse, the data is not observational in a usable way: the closed-loop controller has already compensated for the disturbance, so the recorded correlation between the setpoint and the outcome is inverted relative to the physics. Feed that to a correlation engine and it will confidently recommend moving the parameter in the wrong direction. Causal answers in a plant come from designed experiments, and a DOE costs production time that nobody has budgeted. A digital twin in the engineering sense — a calibrated, validated physics model — is a multi-year instrumentation project, not a visualisation layer, and it is worth asking which of the two is in the proposal.

where_it_does_not.claim: AI in the safety function, or closed-loop autonomous control writing setpoints to the PLC
where_it_does_not.why_not: There is no practical route to sign it off. Functional safety assessment for machinery rests on deterministic, analysable behaviour with a demonstrated performance level or safety integrity level; the machinery safety standards offer no accepted method for demonstrating that for a learned model, and EU machinery law now singles out safety components with self-evolving machine-learning behaviour for mandatory notified-body involvement rather than self-certification. No safety integrator will put their name on a PL d or PL e function containing a learned model, and no plant manager will accept unbounded model output writing to a PLC that moves a press. Advisory output to an operator, or a bounded recommendation a human enters, is a different and permissible thing — but it is not what the autonomous-control pitch is selling.

where_it_does_not.claim: Vision inspection with no training data — a foundation model that spots anomalies out of the box
where_it_does_not.why_not: It finds gross anomalies, which you were already catching. It fails precisely where the money is: at the accept line. Your escapes and your false rejects both live in the narrow band where a blemish is marginally inside or outside the boundary sample, and that line is a business decision specific to your customer and your part — it is not recoverable from general visual priors, and unsupervised anomaly scoring has no mechanism for learning it. Expect a beautiful demonstration on obvious defects and then an unusable false-reject rate on the real mix, at which point someone widens the threshold until it passes everything.

where_it_does_not.claim: AI that replaces inspection or QMS headcount by grading parts to specification
where_it_does_not.why_not: Inspection is a contractual and regulatory artefact before it is a technical one. Your control plan and PPAP name the method and the gauge; in automotive supply, changing an inspection method is a process change requiring customer notification and, commonly, re-submission. In a medical device or aerospace plant it triggers validation and change control. So the automated station does not replace the documented method — it runs alongside it until it is formally qualified, with a measurement systems analysis it must actually pass (for a pass/fail vision decision that is an attribute agreement study against known parts, not a variable gauge R&R), and the headcount stays for that whole period. Any business case that books the saving from month one is wrong by the length of that qualification, which is measured in months, not weeks.

where_it_does_not.claim: Generative AI that writes your PLC, robot or CNC code, or 'self-optimising' control logic on a running machine
where_it_does_not.why_not: Control code is not validated by reading it; it is validated by commissioning on the real machine, and the failure modes that matter — an inverted interlock, a permissive that latches, a race between scan cycles, a safety-rated output treated as a standard one — are invisible in plausible-looking ladder or structured text and only appear when something moves. There is no cheap test harness: your test bed is production hardware, and a wrong output energises an axis next to a person. Add change control, the OEM's licensing terms on their own code, and the fact that a modification to the control system can pull the machine back into a conformity assessment, and the honest scope shrinks to offline drafting of non-safety routines that an engineer reviews line by line and commissions normally — which saves typing, not engineering.

preconditions: A part identity that survives the whole route. Genealogy from serial or lot back through component lots, line, shift and build date, resolvable in one query. Almost every application above degrades to an anecdote without it, and most plants discover the breaks only when they try.

A defined data path off the plant floor that the OT side owns and agrees to. In practice that means a read-only historian or broker replica in a demilitarised zone, the flow going outward only, and no analytics component holding a route to a PLC. Treat it as a new conduit in the 62443 sense and get it risk-assessed as one. If the answer to "how does the model get the data" is a laptop on the control network, stop — that is a bigger risk than any benefit on this page.

Maintenance work orders coded to failure mode, with a date for the functional failure distinct from the date the job was closed. Count the coded events before anyone builds anything. This single precondition decides whether predictive maintenance is real here or theatre.

A defect taxonomy that one person owns, with boundary samples that reflect it, and agreement in advance on what happens when the model and the inspector disagree. Without a decided tiebreak rule, every ambiguous part becomes a negotiation and the station loses authority within weeks.

Acceptance criteria agreed before the build — the escape rate, false-reject rate or accuracy the system must hold, how it will be measured, and who signs that it passed. Without a number agreed in advance, the pilot is scored on impressions and will be declared a success either way.

A system of record that can receive the output — MES, QMS or ERP — and a workflow that changes because of it. Output that lands only on a dashboard changes nothing and will be switched off at the first licence renewal.

An export control determination made before any drawing, process specification, machine parameter or image leaves the building. Whether the technical data is ITAR- or EAR-controlled, which foreign persons on the project would be receiving a release, and whether the chosen hosting satisfies the encryption and access conditions. This is a legal determination, not an IT one, and retrofitting it is expensive.

Change control that treats a model update as a process change, and a named owner for each deployed model with a written rule for when it is switched off. A retrained inspection model is a new inspection method; in a regulated or customer-audited plant it needs the same revalidation, documentation and approval as any other change to the control plan. Agree that before the first model ships, not at the first audit.

regulation.name: ITAR — International Traffic in Arms Regulations
regulation.citation: 22 CFR Parts 120–130; encryption carve-out at 22 CFR 120.54(a)(5)
regulation.what_it_requires: If you make or support items on the US Munitions List, the technical data required for their design, production, manufacture, assembly, operation, repair or modification — drawings, process specifications, machine parameters, inspection imagery of controlled geometry — is itself controlled. Releasing it to a foreign person, including inside the United States, is an export. Sending, taking or storing it outside the US is not treated as an export only where the data is unclassified and secured end-to-end with cryptographic modules compliant with FIPS 140-2 or its successors (or comparable strength, at least AES-128), the means of decryption is never provided to any third party including the hosting provider, and it is not intentionally sent to or stored in a country subject to the ITAR arms embargo list or Russia. Standard commercial AI services where the provider can read the plaintext do not meet that condition. This constrains which AI services you may use at all, and who may see the training data and the model output.

regulation.name: EAR deemed exports — Export Administration Regulations
regulation.citation: 15 CFR 734.13(b) (deemed export); encryption provision at 15 CFR 734.18(a)(5) and (b); Commerce Control List at Supplement No. 1 to 15 CFR Part 774
regulation.what_it_requires: Releasing controlled technology or source code to a foreign person in the United States is a deemed export to that person's most recent country of citizenship or permanent residency. For a plant with a mixed-nationality engineering team, giving a model — or a contractor tuning it — access to controlled process technology is an export event requiring analysis and potentially a licence. The EAR carries an encrypted-transmission and storage provision analogous to the ITAR one, with its own FIPS-based conditions; read it directly rather than assuming the two regimes match. Classification against the Commerce Control List comes first: the analysis is worthless until someone has determined the ECCN of the technology in question.

regulation.name: CMMC and safeguarding of Controlled Unclassified Information
regulation.citation: 32 CFR Part 170 (CMMC Program, effective 16 December 2024); DFARS 252.204-7012; CMMC contract clause DFARS 252.204-7021, added by the acquisition rule published 10 September 2025 and effective 10 November 2025
regulation.what_it_requires: Defence suppliers handling Controlled Unclassified Information must implement the NIST SP 800-171 safeguarding requirements as incorporated by DFARS 252.204-7012 (which also carries the 72-hour cyber incident reporting duty and flow-down to subcontractors) and, where the CMMC clause is in the contract, hold the assessment level it specifies. Any AI system that ingests CUI — drawings, process data, quality records on defence parts — sits inside that boundary and inherits the full control set: access control, audit, incident reporting, and flow-down to the service provider. A cloud AI service outside an assessed boundary is the fastest way to put a contract at risk. The phase-in has moved more than once, including a Department of Defense class deviation in 2026 that paused the second phase while self-assessment obligations and SPRS scoring continued; treat any published timeline, this one included, as out of date and check the specific solicitation and the current deviation text.

regulation.name: EU AI Act, read together with the Machinery Regulation
regulation.citation: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Article 6(1) and Annex I, as amended in 2026 by the digital omnibus amending regulation; Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (Machinery Regulation), applying from 20 January 2027
regulation.what_it_requires: An AI system that is a safety component of machinery is regulated in both frames at once. The Machinery Regulation lists safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning that ensure safety functions, and machinery embedding them, in the Annex I Part A category that loses the self-certification route: notified body involvement is mandatory even where harmonised standards are applied in full. Under the AI Act, such a system is high-risk by the Annex I product route, with the associated risk management, data governance, logging, transparency and human oversight obligations. The application date for the Annex I route was deferred during 2026 and now runs later than the rest of the AI Act — confirm the current dates and the final amending text with counsel rather than relying on any published summary, including this one. For most plants the practical reading is simpler: keep learned models out of the safety function and out of the CE-marking argument.

regulation.name: FDA Quality Management System Regulation (medical device manufacturing)
regulation.citation: 21 CFR Part 820, as amended by the QMSR final rule, in effect since 2 February 2026, incorporating ISO 13485:2016 by reference; electronic records at 21 CFR Part 11
regulation.what_it_requires: Device manufacturers must operate a quality management system meeting ISO 13485:2016 plus FDA's additional requirements in Part 820. Software used in the quality system and software used in production or service provision must be validated for its intended use before use and revalidated on change — ISO 13485 clauses 4.1.6 and 7.5.6 — with the approach documented and proportionate to risk. An AI inspection station that makes an accept or reject decision is production software under this regime: it needs a validation protocol, defined acceptance criteria, and a change-control path that treats retraining as a change requiring revalidation. If its output is the quality record, Part 11 controls on electronic records, audit trails and signatures apply.

regulation.name: OSHA machine guarding and control of hazardous energy
regulation.citation: 29 CFR 1910.212 (general machine guarding); 29 CFR 1910.147 (control of hazardous energy)
regulation.what_it_requires: Point-of-operation hazards must be guarded, and servicing or maintenance requires energy isolation under a documented lockout/tagout programme. Two consequences for AI projects: installing cameras, sensors or new automation must not defeat, bypass or obstruct an existing guard or interlock, and any system that could initiate machine motion — including a scheduling or control integration — must be reconciled with the energy-control procedure before it goes live, with the procedure updated and employees retrained. Retrofits that quietly change when a machine can start are the common way this is breached, and the finding lands on the employer, not the integrator.

regulation.name: Functional safety standards for machinery and robots
regulation.citation: Described, not cited by clause — ISO 13849-1, IEC 62061, and ISO 10218-1 and -2 in their 2025 editions for industrial robots
regulation.what_it_requires: These are the standards normally used to demonstrate that a machinery safety function is adequate, and in the EU the harmonised versions carry a presumption of conformity — check the current Official Journal list for which editions are cited, as it lags publication. They require safety functions to have analysable, deterministic behaviour with a demonstrated performance level or safety integrity level, and they provide no accepted method for validating a learned model in that role. The practical requirement is that a learned model may inform an operator and may not be the safety function. The industrial robot standards were substantially revised in 2025 and now absorb the collaborative-operation content previously held in a technical specification; if you are integrating collaborative or fenceless cells, work from the current edition rather than the 2011 one your integrator may still be using.

regulation.name: Automotive and aerospace customer quality requirements
regulation.citation: Described, not cited by clause — IATF 16949:2016 with the AIAG core tools (APQP, PPAP, MSA, FMEA); AS9100 and AS9102 first-article inspection in aerospace
regulation.what_it_requires: These are contractual rather than statutory, and in practice they bite harder than statute. The control plan defines the inspection method for each characteristic; changing it is a process change requiring customer notification and typically re-submission, and customer-specific requirements often go further than the standard. Any measurement or inspection system must pass a measurement systems analysis before it can be relied on for disposition — an AI vision station is a measurement system and must be studied as one, which for a pass/fail decision means an attribute agreement study against known parts, repeated across lighting conditions, shifts and operators. Aerospace adds first-article requirements and configuration control that make an undocumented model change a finding. IATF 16949:2016 remains the current edition; a second edition is in preparation with publication signalled for 2027, so build change control that can absorb it.

regulation.name: OT network security and EU network security obligations
regulation.citation: Described, not cited by clause for the standards — ISA/IEC 62443 series for industrial automation and control system security; Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2) for EU entities
regulation.what_it_requires: The 62443 series defines the zone-and-conduit model that most plant networks are built on, with defined security levels per zone and controlled conduits between them. Any data path created for an AI project is a new conduit and must be specified, risk-assessed, monitored and documented as one. For manufacturers in scope of NIS2 — the directive lists several manufacturing sub-sectors, including computers and electronics, electrical equipment, machinery, motor vehicles and medical devices, as important entities above the size thresholds — risk management measures, supply chain security and incident reporting duties apply at entity level, with personal accountability for management. Reporting runs on short clocks measured in hours after awareness of a significant incident. NIS2 is a directive: the binding text is your national transposition, and it varies by country, so confirm scope and duties for each country you operate in.

regulation.name: Product defect reporting duties triggered by what your analytics find
regulation.citation: Consumer products: 15 U.S.C. 2064(b) with the reporting rules at 16 CFR Part 1115. Motor vehicles and equipment: 49 U.S.C. 30118(c), with early warning reporting at 49 CFR Part 579
regulation.what_it_requires: This is the entry most often missed when buying warranty analytics. Consumer product manufacturers must report immediately to the CPSC on obtaining information reasonably supporting the conclusion that a product contains a defect that could create a substantial product hazard or an unreasonable risk of serious injury; the rules treat "immediately" as a matter of hours, not weeks, and the safe course is to report while still investigating. Vehicle and equipment manufacturers must notify NHTSA within five working days of a determination that a safety-related defect exists, and separately file periodic early warning data on claims and field reports. An emerging-issue detector is a knowledge-generating machine: it moves the date on which you are deemed to have known, and therefore the date the clock started. Build the escalation route to counsel before the model goes live, and document how signals are triaged — the log will be read later by someone unsympathetic.

sectors.economics: Take a single vision inspection cell as the honest unit. The model is the cheapest part of it. The majority of first-cost is mechanical and optical — fixturing that presents the part the same way every cycle, lighting chosen for the defect physics, guarding, a reject mechanism and confirmation that the part actually left the line, and the PLC integration to trigger and act on the result. Budget the engineering hours for that as the main line item and the software as a minority of it. Then add the costs that appear in no proposal. First, sample generation: you need defective parts across the range, including marginal ones, and on a capable process you will have to deliberately produce them, which costs scheduled production time and scrap. Second, labelling and adjudication — a few thousand images labelled by someone whose judgement the plant accepts, not by a cheap annotation service that has never seen the boundary board. Third, integration into the system of record, which is where most projects stall: writing the result against the serial in MES so it becomes part of the quality record rather than a number on a screen. Fourth, the OT work — the historian or broker replica, the DMZ, the firewall changes, per-tag historian licensing if you are adding tags, and a security review that will take longer than you expect because the people who run that network are correct to be conservative. Fifth, qualification, which is usually the schedule driver rather than the build: the measurement systems analysis, the customer notification or re-submission where the control plan changes, and the period in which the manual method runs in parallel because the documented method has not yet been changed. Budget that parallel run in months. Sixth, the human review that does not go away: inspectors become adjudicators of flagged parts and auditors of escape rate. Seventh, model governance as an annual cost, not a project cost: validation protocol and acceptance criteria, revalidation on every retrain, documentation an IATF, FDA or customer auditor will ask to see, and version records showing which model made which disposition on which date. Eighth, ongoing retraining — new part numbers, a new supplier, seasonal material variation — which in practice means a standing fraction of an engineer's time for the life of the cell, and if nobody owns it the cell degrades quietly rather than failing loudly. Finally, price the failure mode, because it is asymmetric. A false reject costs you a good part and some margin. An escape costs containment: sorting at the customer's plant, premium freight, a line-down charge that in automotive is billed by the hour at a rate designed to hurt, and a customer quality score that follows you into the next sourcing round. In a device or aerospace plant it costs a deviation, a possible field action, and a finding at the next audit. That asymmetry is the reason the sensible design point is a model tuned to over-flag with fast human adjudication, and the reason a business case built on removing the human is usually a business case built on a risk nobody priced. As a planning order of magnitude rather than a quotation: a first cell, all-in with integration and qualification, is a mid-six-figure programme in a regulated plant and materially less in a simple one — an estimate, dependent on line speed, defect complexity, and how much of your document and data groundwork already exists. The second cell on the same line costs a fraction of the first; the first cell in a different plant does not, because the fixturing, the taxonomy and the qualification start again.
sectors.first_step: Pull every maintenance work order for one asset class — one machine type you have several of — for the last twenty-four months, and count three numbers by hand. How many are genuine functional failures rather than planned PM or minor adjustment. How many of those carry a coded failure mode rather than free text. And how many distinct examples you have of the single most common mode, dated to when the asset actually failed rather than when the job was closed. That third number is the one that decides everything. If it is in the single digits — and in most plants it is — predictive maintenance on that asset class is not a modelling project this year, it is a failure-coding and work-order discipline project, and knowing that before you sign reorders the whole roadmap in favour of inspection, supplier documents and warranty text, which run on data you already possess. The count takes an afternoon and no software, and it is the same afternoon that tells you whether the vendor in front of you asked to see it.

sectors.label: Construction and contracting
sectors.lede: Construction runs on a document trail that has to hold up years later: the submittal log, the RFI register, the current set, the daily reports, the pay application and its waivers. Almost all of the useful AI in this sector works on that trail — reading it, reconciling it, finding what contradicts what — and almost all of the AI that disappoints here promises prediction instead, because every job is a new company with a new team on a new site, and eleven jobs is not a training set. The firms that get value are the ones whose document control was already disciplined; the technology makes a good register faster and a bad register confidently wrong.

where_it_helps.name: Submittal register build and specification reconciliation
where_it_helps.the_work: A project engineer reads the spec book at buyout and builds the submittal log — every product data sheet, shop drawing, sample, mock-up and delegated-design item each technical section calls for, with the responsible sub against each one and the Division 01 procedural requirements sitting over the top. On a mid-size commercial job this is a week of somebody's life, and what gets missed at buyout surfaces as a late submittal six months later, usually on a long-lead package.
where_it_helps.what_it_does: Reads the specification sections and extracts the submittal requirements into a draft register — section number, article, item description, submittal type, and the trade package it belongs to — then reconciles that draft against the log as it actually exists and lists what the spec requires and the log does not contain. Useful variants also separate deferred and delegated-design submittals, and the closeout items (O&M data, warranties, attic stock) that nobody builds a log for until turnover.
where_it_helps.what_it_needs: The conformed specification set as text-bearing PDFs, not scans of scans, with every addendum and post-award clarification loaded alongside it; the MasterFormat-division-to-subcontract mapping your firm actually uses rather than the generic one; and write access to the project management system holding the log. Someone must own the register afterwards.
where_it_helps.what_it_saves: Estimate, and it scales with the size of the spec book: the first-pass build drops from days to hours, with a reviewer still walking the whole list. The larger recovery is the missed item found at buyout rather than at delivery — that one is real but not schedulable, so do not put it in a business case.
where_it_helps.failure_mode: It reconciles against the wrong version of the spec. Addenda and post-award clarifications change submittal requirements, and a register built from the bid set silently omits them. It also over-extracts: every cross-reference to Section 01 33 00 becomes a line item, and a reviewer who trusts the output ends up chasing submittals nobody wants, which is how a project team learns to stop reading the tool's list.

where_it_helps.name: Drawing revision delta detection across issued sets
where_it_helps.the_work: When a bulletin, ASI or revised IFC set lands, someone has to determine what actually changed on each sheet, decide which trades are affected, and push the change to the field before work proceeds on superseded information. Revision clouds and delta triangles are supposed to tell you this. They are frequently wrong, incomplete or absent, and the ones that matter most — a dimension string, a detail callout, a slab depression — are the easiest to leave uncloud.
where_it_helps.what_it_does: Aligns two versions of the same sheet and identifies geometric and annotation differences independently of the revision clouds, then describes the change in words a superintendent can use and flags which trades it touches. The underlying overlay-and-compare function is old and deterministic; the part that is new is the written characterisation and the trade routing, and that is the part to distrust.
where_it_helps.what_it_needs: A controlled current set with unambiguous version identity — sheet number, revision, issue date — and vector PDFs where possible. Scanned or rasterised sheets degrade this badly. It also needs somebody whose job is maintaining currency, because the tool compares what you give it. It does not solve trade-coordination overlay, which is a different problem in a different tool.
where_it_helps.what_it_saves: Estimate: the comparison itself goes from roughly an hour a sheet to minutes, on sets that run to hundreds of sheets. The real value is catching an unclouded change, which is a rework avoidance, and rework avoidance cannot be forecast honestly.
where_it_helps.failure_mode: False negatives on dimension-string and detail-reference changes, which are exactly the ones that cost money. It also cannot tell you a change is significant — moving a slab edge two inches and moving a general note both register as differences. Treat the output as a worklist for a human, never as a change notice, and never as the basis for a claim that the change was or was not a change in scope.

where_it_helps.name: RFI triage, duplicate detection and first-draft response routing
where_it_helps.the_work: An incoming RFI has to be read, classified, checked against what has already been asked and answered, routed to whoever can answer it, and tracked against the contractual response window — commonly seven or fourteen days, and the days matter because an unanswered RFI is the spine of a delay argument. The register on a large job runs to several hundred items, a meaningful share of which are re-asks of something already closed, often by a different sub in a different trade.
where_it_helps.what_it_does: Matches a new RFI against the closed register and surfaces near-duplicates with the prior answer attached; classifies it (design clarification, field condition, coordination conflict, substitution request) and proposes a routing; drafts a response where the answer already exists in the record, for a human to accept, edit or reject.
where_it_helps.what_it_needs: The full RFI history in one place, including the attachments, the marked-up sketches and the answers, not just the subject lines. Cross-project history helps only where your spec and detailing conventions are stable, which for most contractors means only within a repeat owner or a repeat prototype.
where_it_helps.what_it_saves: Estimate, and measure your own rather than importing one. The per-RFI cost figures that circulate in this industry trace back to a small number of studies published over a decade ago; quoting them to a CFO invites the question of where they came from, and the honest answer is that they do not describe your projects. The defensible arithmetic is local: pull the last closed job's register, count the items that were re-asks of something already answered, multiply by what a reviewer hour costs you fully loaded, and treat duplicate suppression as recovering some fraction of that. Response-time compression on the contractual clock is the bigger prize and is not expressible as a dollar figure in advance.
where_it_helps.failure_mode: It marks a genuinely new question as a duplicate because the wording matches, and the prior answer is applied to a different location with a different condition. Any suppressed RFI must still appear in the register as raised-and-closed with the reason, because an RFI that never existed is an RFI you cannot point to when the delay analysis is run three years later.

where_it_helps.name: Assembling the contemporaneous record for change-order exposure
where_it_helps.the_work: A PM prices a change and writes the narrative. The hard part is not the pricing — it is reconstructing when the condition was first observed, what the daily reports say about crews standing by, which RFI or ASI it traces to, whether the schedule update for that period shows the activity on the critical path, and whether written notice went out inside the contractual window. On standard general conditions that window can be short, and blowing it converts an entitlement into an argument.
where_it_helps.what_it_does: Given a date range and a location, activity or cost code, pulls the daily reports, RFIs, correspondence, meeting minutes, photographs, delivery tickets and schedule updates that touch it, and produces a dated chronology with links back to source documents — the raw material for the narrative, and for the notice-date question.
where_it_helps.what_it_needs: Daily reports that were actually filled in, correspondence held in the project system rather than in individual mailboxes and phones, and date and location metadata that is trustworthy. This is the precondition that most often fails, and it fails quietly.
where_it_helps.what_it_saves: Estimate: chronology assembly that takes a PM two to three days, or a claims consultant considerably longer at consultant rates, compresses to a working session. On a job with a dozen contested changes the arithmetic is significant. It saves nothing at all where the daily reports are one line long.
where_it_helps.failure_mode: Silent omission. The chronology looks complete and is missing the one email that establishes notice, because it lived in somebody's personal mailbox or a text thread. A chronology that appears authoritative and is incomplete is worse than no chronology, because the PM stops looking. And everything the tool reads, retrieves and writes is discoverable — assume opposing counsel will ask how the chronology was assembled and what was excluded.

where_it_helps.name: Pay-application compliance pre-flight: waivers, certified payroll, insurance
where_it_helps.the_work: Before a draw goes out, somebody checks that every tier has returned the right conditional or unconditional waiver in the right statutory form for the right period and amount, that certified payroll is in for the covered weeks on public work, that certificates of insurance and any required endorsements have not lapsed, and that retainage is calculated the way this contract says rather than the way the last job said.
where_it_helps.what_it_does: Extracts the structured fields from returned documents — claimant, through-date, amount, waiver type, project and job identifiers — and checks them against the schedule of values and the sub ledger, then lists exceptions. On the certified payroll side it checks classification, hours and fringe entries against the applicable wage determination before submission rather than after an audit. The rule-checking half of this is deterministic and long-established; the document-extraction half in front of it is the newer and weaker half, and the split is worth understanding before you buy.
where_it_helps.what_it_needs: A clean subcontract ledger with tiers, the applicable wage determination for the contract, the governing statutory waiver forms for each jurisdiction you work in, and a rule set that encodes this contract's retainage terms rather than your default ones.
where_it_helps.what_it_saves: Estimate: for a contractor processing several hundred waivers a month, the visible saving is AP and project-accounting time, on the order of a clerk-week a month at that volume. The larger avoided cost is the draw rejected on a defective package and the month of float that follows.
where_it_helps.failure_mode: It accepts a waiver whose wording departs from the statutory form. Several jurisdictions prescribe the exact language, and a non-conforming waiver may be ineffective to release the lien right you believed you had released — a checker pattern-matching on 'looks like a waiver' will pass it. Extraction confidence on handwritten, faxed and photographed documents is poor, and those come from exactly the subs you worry about. Never let it auto-release a payment; it produces an exception list for a human who signs.

where_it_helps.name: Safety observation triage from field photography
where_it_helps.the_work: A superintendent walks the deck and writes observations. A safety manager reviews photographs from daily reports and 360 captures looking for unprotected leading edge, missing or unattached fall protection, ladder misuse, unshored or unbenched excavation, damaged rigging and slings, housekeeping and silica controls. Coverage is a function of how many hours a human can look at pictures.
where_it_helps.what_it_does: Flags candidate hazards in field photography and routes them to the responsible contractor for correction, building a timestamped observation record. Detection quality varies enormously by hazard class: PPE-on-a-person and obvious guardrail gaps are the tractable end; whether an excavation is properly benched for its soil class, whether a sling is rated for the pick, whether a scaffold was tagged, are not visible in a photograph and should not be claimed.
where_it_helps.what_it_needs: Consistent photo capture with location metadata, a defined correction workflow with named owners and a stated response time, and a written policy — agreed in advance with counsel — on who reviews flags, how fast, and what is retained.
where_it_helps.what_it_saves: Estimate: coverage rather than headcount. It looks at every photograph rather than a sample. Do not model it as replacing a safety manager's walk — nobody has demonstrated that, and the walk does things a photograph cannot, starting with talking to the crew.
where_it_helps.failure_mode: Two, pointing in opposite directions. False positives at volume train the field to ignore the feed within weeks, and a feed the field ignores is worse than none. And a controlling employer that has generated a documented, timestamped flag it did not act on has manufactured its own evidence of knowledge — under OSHA's multi-employer citation policy a general contractor can be cited for a subcontractor's hazard it had authority to correct, and an unactioned flag sitting in your own system cuts directly against a reasonable-care defence. Design the programme around closure, not detection. Separately, observation systems tied to crew scorecards or incentives can operate as a deterrent to injury reporting, which is its own violation, and monitoring of workers sits close to protected activity under federal labour law whatever your intent.

where_it_helps.name: Autonomous progress tracking from reality capture
where_it_helps.the_work: Quantifying percent-complete for the pay application and the schedule update, currently done by a superintendent and a project engineer walking the job with the schedule of values and arguing about it with the owner's rep.
where_it_helps.what_it_does: Compares periodic laser scan or 360 walk data against the model or schedule and reports installed quantities and progress by area and system.
where_it_helps.what_it_needs: A model actually maintained at the level of detail being measured, disciplined weekly capture of the whole job including above ceilings and inside walls before closure, and someone to reconcile the output against the schedule of values line by line.
where_it_helps.what_it_saves: Estimate, and the honest answer for most projects is very little, because the walk still happens and the reconciliation is new work. On structure and envelope on a large repetitive building it can be real.
where_it_helps.failure_mode: It is sold as objective percent-complete for pay applications and does not survive contact with one. It measures what it can see, so rough-in behind closed walls, procurement and stored materials, and anything MEP above a closed ceiling are invisible or wrong; the model drifts from the as-built within weeks of the first field change; and an owner's rep will not accept a machine number over a walk. Firms buy it for pay-app automation and end up using it as a dated visual archive of conditions — genuinely useful in a claim, and not what they paid for.

where_it_does_not.claim: Machine-learned schedule risk prediction — 'our model tells you which activities will slip, trained on your historical project data'
where_it_does_not.why_not: The data does not exist in the form the method requires. A contractor with a good decade of records has perhaps fifty to two hundred completed jobs, each with a different owner, design team, subcontractor list, labour market, site and weather — closer to two hundred single-observation experiments than a dataset. The CPM logic is hand-built by a scheduler, so activity coding, granularity and constraint style vary by whoever built it; the same wall goes in as one activity on one job and nine on another. Worse, the label is endogenous: 'late' is measured against a baseline that gets re-baselined precisely when things go wrong, so the model learns your re-baselining habits rather than your delivery risk. What does work here is not machine learning at all — Monte Carlo over a duration-uncertainty range that a human assigns, which has been available for thirty years and still requires a scheduler who knows the job.

where_it_does_not.claim: AI estimating that prices a job from the drawings
where_it_does_not.why_not: The price is not in the drawings. Quantity is in the drawings, and quantity extraction from a well-built model is a solved deterministic problem that predates this technology. The price is in what your subs will bid this quarter, which of them is hungry, your own crew composition and productivity, escalation on the long-lead packages, and the general conditions you will actually carry. Those live in a market, not a document. And the historical cost data that would anchor unit pricing is coded to cost codes your own PMs apply inconsistently — the same scope lands in three different codes across three jobs, so 'our historical actuals' are not comparable to each other, let alone to a new job. Tools that assist takeoff by proposing counts and lengths for a human to verify are a genuine convenience and should be bought as that, at that price.

where_it_does_not.claim: Contract risk scoring — upload the prime contract and get your risk position
where_it_does_not.why_not: Your risk position is not in the prime contract. It is in the prime as modified by the owner's supplementary conditions, plus the exhibits, plus what flows down into your subcontracts and what conspicuously does not, plus the course of dealing on this job with this owner's rep. A tool reading the prime alone will tell you a clause is onerous without knowing you failed to flow it down, which is the actual exposure. Notice provisions in particular turn on facts, not text — the clause says twenty-one days from the event, and the whole question is when the event occurred and what you knew, which is in the daily reports. Clause extraction and comparison against your own playbook is useful and real; a composite risk score is theatre, and no general counsel will rely on one or want it sitting in the file when the dispute arrives.

where_it_does_not.claim: Algorithmic subcontractor prequalification scoring
where_it_does_not.why_not: The inputs are thin and self-reported: a financial statement of uncertain vintage, a bonding letter, an EMR, a safety record whose completeness depends on how honestly the sub records, and reference projects the sub chose. There is not enough signal to justify a score carrying a decimal point, and the score will be used as a gate. On public work it also puts you in a position you will have to explain: if a model systematically down-ranks smaller, newer or minority- and women-owned firms because they have shorter histories and thinner balance sheets, you have built a mechanism working against participation goals you are contractually committed to, and on federally assisted work the good-faith-efforts record is reviewable. Structured data collection, expiry tracking and exception flags on prequal packages are worth doing. Ranking subs by a number is not.

where_it_does_not.claim: A conversational assistant over the project documents, used as the answer
where_it_does_not.why_not: Retrieval over a construction document set is approximate, and the documents are the contract. The specific failure is currency: the model retrieves a passage from a superseded sheet or a spec section an addendum amended, and answers confidently because nothing in the retrieved text says it has been superseded. In this sector a wrong answer about what the documents require is not an inconvenience — it is built work that has to come out, and an argument about who pays for the removal. The tooling is genuinely useful as a finding aid, for locating where something is addressed so a human opens the actual sheet and reads it. Sold as a source of answers rather than a finding aid, it is a liability that arrives with a plausible tone.

preconditions: One controlled current set with unambiguous supersession. Before anything reads your drawings, the organisation must be able to answer, without a conversation, which revision of a given sheet is current and what superseded it. Most of the failure modes above reduce to a tool reading a sheet that is no longer the sheet.

A named owner for every register. The submittal log, the RFI register, the change log, the waiver file — each needs one person accountable for its state, not a role shared across three PMs. An unowned process cannot be handed to a machine, because there is nobody to notice when the machine is wrong.

Daily reports that are actually written. Everything useful about change-order exposure, delay and safety depends on a contemporaneous field record with dates, crews, locations, weather and conditions. Where the daily report is one sentence, no technology recovers what was not written down — and that is a management problem to fix first, on its own merits.
A cost-code structure applied the same way by every PM on every job. Without it, historical actuals are not comparable across projects, and every claim about learning from your own data is unfounded.

Project correspondence held in the project system rather than in individual mailboxes and phones. Notice, direction and acceleration arguments are lost in personal inboxes and text threads, and a tool that assembles a chronology from the project system will produce a confident, incomplete one.

A written position on confidentiality and data rights before any owner's drawings or models leave your systems. Owner agreements frequently restrict disclosure of project documents to third parties, and sending a set to an external service may breach that whether or not anyone notices. Settle in writing: whether the vendor trains on your content, where it is stored, who owns outputs, and what happens on termination.

Retention and legal-hold discipline extended to cover the new tooling. Prompts, retrieved passages and generated drafts are records. They will be requested in a claim, and 'the software wrote it' is not a position. Decide what is logged, for how long, and how it is placed on hold when a claim is reasonably anticipated.

A licensure line nobody crosses. No machine-generated drawing, calculation or specification goes out under a professional seal unless a licensee was in responsible charge of its preparation. Reviewing a finished output is not responsible charge in most jurisdictions' framing, and the seal is personal to the licensee, not to the firm.

regulation.name: Davis-Bacon and Related Acts — weekly certified payroll and Statement of Compliance
regulation.citation: 29 C.F.R. § 5.5(a)(3)(ii)(A)–(B); Form WH-347 (optional)
regulation.what_it_requires: On covered federal and federally assisted construction, the contractor submits weekly certified payrolls covering the preceding week to the contracting agency, and the prime contractor is responsible for the submission of its subcontractors' payrolls. Each payroll must be accompanied by a signed Statement of Compliance certifying that the payrolls are correct and complete and that each labourer and mechanic was paid not less than the applicable prevailing wage and fringe for the classification of work actually performed. Form WH-347 is optional; any format carrying the required information and the prescribed certification language satisfies it. The certification is signed by a person, and the regulation's own language warns that falsification carries prosecution exposure under 18 U.S.C. § 1001 — which is precisely why automated classification and fringe calculation must be checked by that person before signature, not after.

regulation.name: California statutory lien waiver and release forms
regulation.what_it_requires: Four statutory forms — conditional and unconditional waiver and release, each on progress payment and on final payment — whose language is prescribed by statute; each section requires the document to be in substantially the form it sets out. A waiver departing from the statutory form may be ineffective, meaning a payment made against a defective waiver has not released the lien right you believed it released. Any automated waiver checking must compare against the statutory text, not against a template your firm has been reusing since the last job. Texas and several other states prescribe their own forms; many states prescribe none. This is jurisdiction by jurisdiction and does not generalise.

regulation.name: California public works payroll records and electronic submission
regulation.citation: Cal. Lab. Code §§ 1776, 1771.4
regulation.what_it_requires: Contractors and subcontractors on covered California public works must keep accurate certified payroll records for each worker and furnish them on request; failure to comply within ten days of receipt of a written request carries a penalty of one hundred dollars per worker per calendar day until the records are produced. Records are submitted electronically to the Labor Commissioner through the state's eCPR system on projects subject to DIR compliance monitoring, with awarding bodies and labour compliance programmes commonly imposing weekly submission by contract. Confirm current thresholds, exemptions and enforcement posture with counsel — the registration and eCPR regime has been amended more than once.

regulation.name: OSHA injury and illness reporting, and the anti-deterrence rule
regulation.what_it_requires: Work-related fatalities must be reported to OSHA within eight hours; in-patient hospitalisation, amputation and loss of an eye within twenty-four hours. Separately, an employer must not have any procedure that would deter or discourage a reasonable employee from accurately reporting a work-related injury or illness. That second rule is the one that catches AI safety programmes: an observation or scoring system tied to crew league tables or incentive payments can function as a deterrent to reporting, which is a violation independent of the underlying hazard.

regulation.name: OSHA multi-employer citation policy
regulation.citation: OSHA Directive CPL 02-00-124 (10 December 1999)
regulation.what_it_requires: On a multi-employer worksite more than one employer may be cited for a hazardous condition. A controlling employer — typically the general contractor — may be cited for a subcontractor's hazard it had the authority to correct, measured against a reasonable-care standard rather than the primary employer's standard. This is the governing reason to design AI safety observation around closure rather than detection: a documented, timestamped, unactioned hazard flag is contemporaneous evidence of knowledge, held in your own system, against your own reasonable-care defence.

regulation.name: Miller Act payment bond claims on federal work
regulation.citation: 40 U.S.C. §§ 3131–3134 (bond threshold at § 3131(b); notice and limitation provisions at § 3133(b))
regulation.what_it_requires: A payment bond is required on covered federal construction contracts exceeding one hundred thousand dollars. A claimant with no direct contractual relationship with the prime must give the prime written notice within ninety days of the day it last furnished labour or material, stating with substantial accuracy the amount claimed and the party for whom the work was done, served by a means giving written third-party verification of delivery. Suit on the bond may not be brought until ninety days after last furnishing, and must be brought within one year of that day. These are hard dates keyed to a fact — the last day of furnishing — that lives in daily reports and delivery tickets, which is the argument for making that record navigable rather than merely stored.

regulation.name: Differing site conditions on federal fixed-price construction contracts
regulation.what_it_requires: The contractor must give the contracting officer written notice promptly, and before the conditions are disturbed, of subsurface or latent physical conditions differing materially from those indicated in the contract, or unknown physical conditions of an unusual nature differing materially from those ordinarily encountered. No equitable adjustment is allowed unless that notice was given, and no request is considered after final payment. The companion Changes clause incorporated in the same contract imposes its own short written-notice period for constructive changes — read the clauses as executed rather than as remembered.

regulation.name: Contractual notice windows for claims and concealed conditions
regulation.citation: Described, not cited — read the executed agreement and its supplementary conditions
regulation.what_it_requires: Standard published general conditions impose short notice periods: commonly twenty-one days from the event or from first recognition of the condition for notice of claim, and a shorter window, often around fourteen days from first observance, for concealed or unknown physical conditions. Owners routinely shorten these in supplementary conditions and flow them down at shorter intervals still, and some make notice a condition precedent to entitlement. Never rely on the published form or on what the last job said — read the executed contract, and encode its actual dates into whatever tracks them.

regulation.name: Professional licensure, responsible charge and sealing
regulation.citation: Described, not cited — state engineering and architecture practice acts; the NCEES Model Law is a model, not law in any state
regulation.what_it_requires: Only a licensee may seal engineering or architectural documents, and only where they were prepared by or under that licensee's responsible charge — direct control and personal supervision, with the professional actively engaged in the development of the work. Professional-society and board guidance generally takes the position that reviewing drawings after preparation, without involvement in their development, does not meet the standard. The practical consequence for AI-assisted design and calculation is that generate-then-review is not a licensure-safe workflow, and the definition varies state by state.

regulation.name: Worker monitoring and federal labour law
regulation.citation: National Labor Relations Act § 7 (29 U.S.C. § 157); NLRB General Counsel Memorandum GC 23-02 was rescinded by GC 25-05 (14 February 2025)
regulation.what_it_requires: The General Counsel memorandum setting out an aggressive framework for electronic monitoring and algorithmic management was withdrawn in February 2025, so that framework is not current enforcement policy. Section 7 is unchanged: surveillance of, or creating the impression of surveillance of, protected concerted activity remains unlawful, and it makes no difference that a camera and a model are doing the looking. On union projects, monitoring and its use in discipline may also be a mandatory subject of bargaining. Treat the rescission as a change in enforcement priority, not as permission, and confirm the current position before rollout.

regulation.name: DBE participation and good-faith-efforts documentation on federally assisted transportation work
regulation.citation: 49 C.F.R. Part 26 (good faith efforts at § 26.53; substitution consent at § 26.53(f))
regulation.what_it_requires: On federally assisted highway, transit and airport contracts, recipients set contract goals for Disadvantaged Business Enterprise participation, and a bidder must either meet the goal or document adequate good faith efforts to do so, with the recipient reviewing that documentation. A prime may not terminate or substitute a committed DBE subcontractor without the recipient's prior written consent. Any automated prequalification or selection scoring sits directly across this: you must be able to explain how a sub was screened, and 'the model ranked them low' is an explanation that will be examined rather than accepted.

sectors.economics: The licence is the small number and nobody believes it until they have run a year. Budget the licence at what the vendor quotes, then budget these alongside it, all as mechanisms and orders of magnitude rather than benchmarks. Integration into the systems of record: your project management platform, your accounting and job-cost system, and the owner's platform, which on most jobs is a different one you are contractually obliged to use — it is ordinary for a contractor to be running several owner-mandated platforms concurrently across a portfolio, each integration bespoke. Expect integration and per-project configuration to cost a multiple of the first year's licence, and expect that cost to recur every time an owner mandates a platform you have not connected before. Document currency: the drawing-comparison and document-reading tools are only as good as the answer to 'which sheet is current', and maintaining that is a person — often the person you were hoping to free up. Ongoing human review that does not go away: a submittal still needs a reviewer's initials, a certified payroll still needs a signature from someone carrying personal exposure for the certification, a change-order narrative still needs a PM who will sit for a deposition on it. The work moves from assembly to verification; verification is not obviously cheaper per item, and the honest business case is throughput and coverage rather than headcount. Model governance and records: a retention policy covering prompts, retrieved sources and generated drafts, a record of which version of which tool produced what, and legal hold extended to cover all of it — because in a claim three years out, opposing counsel will ask how the chronology was produced, and 'the software did it' invites a discovery request for everything the software touched. Then the failure mode, which is where the money actually is. A missed contractual notice window converts an entitlement into a negotiation, and on a seven-figure change that is a seven-figure swing. A defective lien waiver in a form-prescribing jurisdiction means a payment made against a release that does not release. A superseded sheet issued to the field is rework, and rework is the one number every contractor already knows how to price. One of these in a year erases several years of tooling savings, which is the argument for spending on verification and document control rather than on capability. The arithmetic depends entirely on your volume, your contract mix and how much public work you carry.
sectors.first_step: Take your last three closed change orders over fifty thousand dollars. For each one, reconstruct from the project record alone two dates: when the firm first had actual knowledge of the condition, and when written notice went out. Note every document you had to open to establish those dates, where each one lived, how many of them were in somebody's personal mailbox, and how long the reconstruction took. Do this by hand, with no tooling. If it takes an afternoon per change order, or if you cannot establish the first date at all from the record, you have found the thing to fix — and no AI reading that record was going to do better than you just did, because it would have been reading the same gaps with more confidence and no hesitation. If it takes twenty minutes because the record is clean and complete, you have found the first process worth automating, and you already know what good output looks like, which is the only position from which you can tell whether a tool is working.

sectors.label: Insurance
sectors.lede: Insurance is the one sector where the question "where does AI belong" already has a partial legal answer, written down, by regulators who will ask you for the documentation. A model that makes or supports a decision affecting a policyholder sits inside the same unfair trade practice and unfair claims settlement statutes that have governed adjusters and underwriters for fifty years, and roughly two dozen jurisdictions have now told carriers in writing what they expect to see when they come and look. The practical consequence is unusual: the constraint on adoption here is almost never the model quality, it is whether you can reconstruct and defend the decision two years later.

where_it_helps.name: Submission triage and clearance in commercial and specialty underwriting
where_it_helps.the_work: An underwriting assistant opens a broker's email, works out which attachments are the ACORD applications, which is the statement of values, which are the loss runs and which is a supplemental. They check clearance — has this account already been submitted, by another broker, is there a broker-of-record issue, did we decline it last year. They re-key the schedule and the loss history into the underwriting workbench, chase the broker for the three fields the ACORD left blank, and score the risk against appetite before the underwriter ever sees it.
where_it_helps.what_it_does: Splits and classifies the attachment bundle, extracts schedule and loss-run fields into a structured submission record, matches the named insured and address against existing accounts and prior submissions for clearance, and scores against written appetite rules so out-of-appetite submissions are declined same-day instead of sitting in a queue for a week.
where_it_helps.what_it_needs: Read access to the submission mailbox, a structured target schema that matches your workbench, a labelled corpus of your own historic submissions (several thousand, spanning the brokers you actually trade with), the clearance database, and a written appetite statement precise enough to be encoded. Crucially: a confidence threshold per field and a human queue for everything below it. Also a decision on what the system is permitted to do unaided — declining out of appetite touches the producer relationship and, in some states, the declination notice machinery, so treat an automated decline as a consumer-facing decision and keep an underwriter's name on it.
where_it_helps.what_it_saves: The mechanism is elapsed time, not headcount. Submissions that currently wait days in an assistant's queue get structured within minutes of arrival, so underwriters quote earlier in the broker's shopping window and decline out-of-appetite risks before spending time on them. Order of magnitude, this is an estimate and depends entirely on submission volume and how much of your book is unstructured broker email: on a book taking hundreds of submissions a week you should expect to recover a meaningful fraction of an assistant's day per underwriting team, and to move quote turnaround by days rather than hours. Treat any vendor number as unverified until you have measured your own current submission-to-quote cycle time.
where_it_helps.failure_mode: Loss runs break it. They arrive in a different layout from every carrier, with inconsistent valuation dates, and the thing that matters — whether a large loss is included, and as of when — is the thing most often missing rather than wrong. Extraction is reliably accurate on the fields nobody prices on (construction type, square footage) and least accurate on the ones that move the rate (roof age, sprinkler status, occupancy, protection class). The second failure is quieter: a wrong total insured value or a missed shock loss flows into the quote, and nobody catches it until the renewal or the claim.

where_it_helps.name: First notice of loss intake structuring
where_it_helps.the_work: An intake representative takes the loss call or reads the portal submission, keys the first notice into the claims system, codes cause of loss and peril, confirms the policy was in force at the date of loss, identifies the vehicles, body parts, structures or lines of coverage implicated, opens the features or exposures, and routes the claim to a desk.
where_it_helps.what_it_does: Transcribes the call, structures the reported facts into the claim system's fields, proposes cause-of-loss and peril codes, extracts the specifics (VIN, location, date and time of loss, parties, injuries reported), and flags mismatches — most usefully a date of loss outside the policy period, an unlisted driver, or a reported cause that does not sit under the coverage part the caller assumed. The transcription and extraction half is solid; the code-proposal half is the weaker one and should be treated as a suggestion the representative confirms, not a default the representative overrides.
where_it_helps.what_it_needs: Call recording and transcription with consent handling that satisfies the recording laws in every state you write — all-party consent states change the script, not just the settings; write access to the claims platform through a supported API rather than screen automation; your own cause-of-loss code set with definitions; and a rule that the insured's own description of the loss is stored verbatim and never replaced by a generated version.
where_it_helps.what_it_saves: The mechanism is that the representative stops typing and starts listening, and that coding errors are caught at intake rather than at closing. Order of magnitude, an estimate: handle time per notice falls by a minute or two, which only matters at volume, and the more valuable effect is the reduction in miscoded claims that have to be reopened or reclassified later. If you do not currently measure your miscoding rate at first notice, you cannot claim this benefit.
where_it_helps.failure_mode: Two specific ones. The free-text loss description is what every downstream reader relies on — the adjuster, the SIU analyst, coverage counsel, and eventually opposing counsel — and a model that tidies the insured's own words destroys the record; keep the verbatim and put the structured version beside it, never over it. Second, cause-of-loss coding feeds reserving and the actuarial triangles. A model that systematically shifts coding between two adjacent perils will quietly distort loss development for years before anyone traces it back.

where_it_helps.name: Subrogation identification and recovery screening
where_it_helps.the_work: An adjuster handling a heavy pending is meant to notice that a third party is liable, evaluate whether recovery is worth pursuing, and refer to the subrogation unit inside the applicable limitation period and, for inter-company matters, inside the arbitration deadlines. In practice referral depends on the adjuster's experience and how many claims are on their desk that month.
where_it_helps.what_it_does: Reads the loss description, police report, repair estimate, photographs and prior claim history, and flags claims with probable third-party liability that have not been referred, ranked by expected net recovery after handling cost. It also re-screens claims already closed without referral where the limitation period is still open.
where_it_helps.what_it_needs: The closed-claim file including documents, not just the structured fields; the subrogation unit's own historic referral and recovery outcomes as labels; the applicable limitation periods by state and claim type encoded so the ranking is by time remaining as well as value; and, decisively, subrogation handler capacity to work the queue it produces.
where_it_helps.what_it_saves: The mechanism is recovery dollars, not handling time: claims that would have closed without referral get referred while recovery is still possible. Be careful with the market figures in circulation for missed subrogation — they are vendor and consultancy estimates, the definitions behind them differ, and none of them are auditable, so do not put one in a business case. The only number worth having is your own: pull a random sample of recently closed first-party files, have an experienced subrogation handler review them cold, and count how many had a recovery opportunity nobody referred. Order of magnitude, an estimate: the return is measured against your existing recovery, and on a large personal auto book a single percentage point of additional recovery is real money.
where_it_helps.failure_mode: The flags pile up in a queue nobody is staffed to work, and referral volume rises while recovered dollars do not — because the binding constraint was subrogation handler capacity, not identification. The second failure is timing: a flag raised at day 400 on a two-year statute is technically inside the limit and practically worthless, because the evidence and the responsible party's carrier relationship have gone cold. Rank by time remaining, not only by expected value. This use case is unusually forgiving in one respect — a false positive costs a review, not a consumer harm — which is exactly why it is a sensible first production deployment.

where_it_helps.name: Organised fraud detection through entity resolution and link analysis
where_it_helps.the_work: An SIU analyst works red-flag indicators on individual claims and tries, largely by memory and spreadsheet, to see the pattern across claims — the same body shop, the same medical provider, the same tow operator, the same bank account or phone number appearing across unrelated claimants. Referrals to SIU come from adjusters who have been trained on indicator lists.
where_it_helps.what_it_does: Resolves entities across claims, policies and payments, builds the network, and surfaces clusters — a provider whose claimants share addresses, a repair facility whose supplements always land just under the reinspection threshold, staged-accident rings visible only as a graph. The 'proven' rating attaches to the graph and entity-resolution technique, which has been in production in large SIUs for well over a decade and is not a recent arrival; it does not attach to the newer language-model layers being sold on top of it, which are early and should be rated separately.
where_it_helps.what_it_needs: Claims, policy, payment and vendor data joined on resolved entities, which means investing in the entity resolution itself — it is the project, not a preliminary; access to industry-shared claims databases and anti-fraud bureaux where your state law and your membership permit; SIU investigators to work the output; and a clear legal line between a model output and an investigation, because the output is an investigative lead and nothing else.
where_it_helps.what_it_saves: The mechanism is that rings are found as rings rather than one claim at a time, and that a single cluster can account for many claims at once. Order of magnitude, an estimate: the return concentrates in a small number of large findings rather than spreading across the book, so measure it as identified organised activity per year against SIU cost, not as a percentage improvement on individual claim leakage.
where_it_helps.failure_mode: A score is not evidence and cannot support a denial or even a delay. Unfair claims settlement practice statutes require a reasonable investigation based on the available information and set standards for prompt communication and payment; a claim parked because a model scored it high, with no investigator actually working it, is an unfair claims practice with a paper trail. The other failure is disparate impact: network features correlate strongly with neighbourhood, provider community and surname, and an SIU referral model that concentrates scrutiny on one population is exactly what a market conduct examiner is now equipped to find. Test the referral population by protected class before you deploy, not after.

where_it_helps.name: Claim complexity routing and severity banding
where_it_helps.the_work: A supervisor or a rules engine decides whether a new claim goes to fast-track, to a general adjuster, or to a major-case or complex unit, and an initial reserve is set. The decision is made on thin information — the first notice — and it determines who handles the claim for its whole life and how much attention it gets.
where_it_helps.what_it_does: Predicts an ultimate incurred band and litigation propensity from first-notice fields, policy characteristics, claimant history and geography, and recommends a desk and an initial reserve range.
where_it_helps.what_it_needs: Several years of closed claims with development, a stable definition of ultimate incurred, an honest account of every change to claim handling guidelines and reserving philosophy in the training window, actuarial sign-off, and monitoring that separates model drift from genuine severity trend. It needs a written rule that a routing recommendation is never visible to the claimant and never the basis of a coverage or payment decision.
where_it_helps.what_it_saves: The mechanism is that complex claims reach experienced adjusters early, when intervention still changes the outcome, and simple claims stop consuming senior capacity. Order of magnitude, an estimate that depends on your current mis-routing rate: the value is in the tail — a small number of claims that would have sat on the wrong desk for months. Do not model this as a handling-cost saving; model it as severity avoidance, and be sceptical of your own measurement, because routing changes the outcome you are trying to measure.
where_it_helps.failure_mode: The model learns your company's past reserving and settlement behaviour, not the cost of the loss. Then it closes the loop: a claim routed to fast-track settles small, which confirms the prediction, which reinforces the routing.
